articles.title: India Economy Update: Moody’s Lifts FY27 Growth Outlook to 7% Amid Global Uncertainty
articles.description: India’s economic outlook has received a fresh boost after Moody’s revised its growth projection for the country. The rating agency has raised its estimate for India’s GDP expansion in the 2026-27 financial year from 6% to 7%, pointing to continued resilience in economic activity despite uncertainty in the global environment. The revision comes after India recorded 7.8% real GDP growth in the first quarter, strengthening attention on the pace of domestic economic activity. Moody’s assessment suggests that India’s growth momentum remains comparatively firm even as geopolitical tensions, including instability in the Middle East, continue to create risks for the global economy. The updated projection also puts the spotlight on India’s position among major emerging economies. Strong domestic demand, economic activity and improving fiscal conditions are among the factors being considered in the broader assessment of the country’s growth prospects. At the same time, the outlook is not without potential challenges. Weather conditions and their impact on food prices remain an important variable for the Indian economy. The assessment prices, geopolitical developments and external economic conditions could also influence India’s growth trajectory during the year. These factors renewed focus on India’s economic performance and its ability to maintain growth momentum amid international uncertainties. The latest outlook will now be closely watched also highlights the possible influence of El Niño-related weather patterns, which could affect agricultural output and consequently food inflation. Global energy prices, geopolitical developments and external economic conditions could also influence India’s growth trajectory during the year. These factors mean that the revised projection remains an estimate rather than a guaranteed outcome.
